title: Regional Economic Impacts of the Transition to Electrified Vehicles in Rio Grande do Sul: An Input-Output Analysis
content: The transition to electric vehicles represents a structural technological shift with significant regional economic implications, particularly in regions with established automotive supply chains. This study assesses the economic impact of the partial substitution of internal combustion engine vehicles by electric vehicles in Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil, using the 2019 regional input-output matrix comprising 117 products and 52 economic activities. The simulation assumes a 20% decline in demand for internal combustion engine vehicles, replaced by electric vehicles produced outside the region. The shock also incorporates effects on complementary products positively and negatively affected, such as electricity, petroleum refining, fuel consumption, auto parts, and maintenance services. The analysis applies the Leontief demand model to estimate direct, indirect, and total effects on output, value added, and the State Value-Added Tax (ICMS), while also contributing a methodological framework for partial wage-based closure to measure the induced effect. The results indicate a reduction of BRL 5.788 billion in regional output, equivalent to 0.66% of the regional total. The decline in value added including the induced effect amounts to BRL 1.2 billion, corresponding to 0.30%. ICMS revenue falls by 1.94%, representing BRL 695 million. The implicit shock multiplier of 1.57 reflects the strong intersectoral integration of the automotive supply chain. The findings highlight the importance of policies that mitigate impacts on value added, income, and public revenues, reinforcing the need to understand the effects of technological transitions on regional productive capacity and fiscal sustainability.
